benefits: Debug invisible characters: escapes reveal exactly which code points are in the text.
Safe for JSON and code: \u escapes never break string syntax.
Handles emoji and rare scripts via surrogate pairs automatically.

faqs.a: Unicode assigns every character a number called a code point. The \uXXXX escape writes that number in four hexadecimal digits, so A (code point 65, hex 41) becomes \u0041.
Some tools, file formats and older systems only handle ASCII safely. Escaped text carries the same characters using only ASCII letters, digits and backslashes, so nothing gets corrupted in transit.
Characters above U+FFFF (most emoji) do not fit in four hex digits, so they are stored as two UTF-16 surrogate halves, each written as its own \uXXXX escape. The pair decodes back to one character.
The decoder only replaces well-formed \u followed by exactly four hex digits. Anything else — like \u12 or \uZZZZ — is left untouched in the output.
The swap button puts the current output into the input box and flips the mode, so you can verify that decoding an encoded string returns the original text.
faqs.q: How do I verify a round-trip?

keyFacts: Unicode gives every character a unique code point number.
The \uXXXX escape writes a code point as four hexadecimal digits.
A is code point 65, which is 0x41 in hex, so it encodes as \u0041.
Characters above U+FFFF (like emoji) encode as two \uXXXX surrogate halves.
Escaped text uses only ASCII characters, so it survives ASCII-only systems.
Decoding reverses the process: each valid escape becomes its character again.

limitations: Only \uXXXX escapes are decoded; \u{...} and \U00...... forms are not handled.
Invalid escapes are passed through unchanged rather than flagged.
Encoding always escapes every character, including plain ASCII letters.
Very long texts make very long escape strings (6 characters per input character).

You type "Hi€" in encode mode.

'H' = code point 72 = 0x48 → \u0048
'i' = code point 105 = 0x69 → \u0069
'€' = code point 8364 = 0x20AC → \u20ac

Output: \u0048\u0069\u20ac (3 escapes, 18 characters).
